text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Consumers continue to spend in Q3, says Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS). (p1)
- Airplane maker Fokker's receivers concerned about progress of talks between economic affairs ministry and Samsung. (p1)
- Trading company Hagemeyer buys remaining 50 pct stake in Asian trading group Cosa Liebermaan. (p1)
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel's Q3 net inches up to Dfl 328 (324) million due to coatings division. (p1)
- Trade unions and works council at credit insurer NCM oppose job cuts. (p4)
- Consultancy bureau Twijnstra Gudde plans international expansion. (p4)
- ASM International's Q3 net plunges 71 pct to Dfl 6.8 million on 28 pct lower turnover. (p4)
- Investment company Robeco develops new investment strategy for big institutional investors. (p13)
VOLKSKRANT
- Sports-only TV channel Sport7, only to be watched with decoder in Amsterdam, sells rights of Netherlands-Wales soccer match to local Amsterdam TV station. (p2)
- Soccer club Feijenoord loses Reebok sponsorship due to bad name of club supporters. (p2)
- Car maker NedCar gets allowance to extend production time from 4,000 to 5,000 hours. (p2)
- Air charter company Martinair takes 40 pct stake in Colombia's Tampa. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Cabinet not prepared to meet parliament's wishes on high-speed rail link (HSL). (p9)
- Engineering sector employers association FME-CWM criticises cabinet over tax relieve measures. (p37)
- Plastics company Schuttersveld books 13 pct higher Q3 net at Dfl 18.3 million. (p39)
TROUW
- Staff of Belgian Philips plant on strike since Tuesday. (p8)
- Wholesaler Schuitema's turnover in first 40 weeks rises 3.4 pct to Dfl 2.416 bn. (p25)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Employment in engineering sector expected to grow 3.5 pct this year. (p11)
- ABN Amro bank expecting to take over Hungary's state bank Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB) this week. (p12)
